_status: MEASURED 2026-09-13/14 on bcc0e09; re-measured 2026-09-15 on 58d7bac (0.4.0). RUN-TO-RUN VARIANCE IS REAL AND IT IS FUSIONCORE'S, NOT THE HARNESS'S. Measured spreads of FusionCore against the RL control on identical input: 2013-04-05 0.17% vs control 0.47% (n=2); 2012-08-20 4.57% vs control 0.00% (n=2); 2012-06-15 5.8% vs control 1.9% (n=7). The control being identical to two decimal places on 2012-08-20 is what rules out the input. A 'background machine load is worth 4.3%' claim written here earlier on 2026-09-15 is WITHDRAWN: idle re-runs moved 2013-04-05 by 0.17% and made 2012-08-20 4.6% WORSE, both wrong for that theory. It came from treating a 2-sample group as a measurement. UNEXPLAINED. Do not propose a mechanism without more n. Untested observation: the two sequences with several percent of variance are the two long-blackout ones, and the one with almost none has the shortest outages. PRACTICAL RULE: a move under ~6% on 2012-06-15 or 2012-08-20 is not evidence of anything. 2013-04-05 repeats tightly enough that ~1% is meaningful there. Always run the RL control and record wall-clock duration beside every result.

2012-06-15.note: Issue #63, one 461 s blackout. Post-blackout recovery went 277 m (no fix) to 111 m (recovery only, continuity gate armed) to 13 m once the continuity history was stopped from spanning the gap. Continuity rejections after the blackout: 18-20 running to the end of the run, down to 1.
2012-06-15.spread_warning: n=7 clean on 58d7bac: 70.86, 70.92, 71.14, 71.31, 73.34, 74.29, 74.95. Spread 5.8%, control 1.9%. One further run at 54.24 is EXCLUDED: 82 min playback where every other run took 55-61, machine suspended mid-run; not a gate flip and not a truncated recording, mechanism never identified. A move under ~6% here means nothing.
2012-06-15.rerun_20261005: CONFIRMED on c263814, 2026-10-05: FusionCore 73.313, RL control 18.489 against the baseline's 18.487, a move of +0.01%, which is as clean as this harness gets and is what makes the FusionCore figure believable. 73.313 sits inside the n=7 cluster (70.86 to 74.95), so this is a third independent confirmation rather than a new value, and the baseline is NOT moved. The published README figure of 49.2 m is wrong by 1.490x. Filter rate 99.9 Hz over 3310 s, 4 rl_ekf update-rate misses.

2012-08-20.note: Issue #64. 120.03 to 116.4, inside the 4.6% spread, so unchanged rather than improved. Its value is as a no-regression check: seven GNSS gaps and an adversarial outlier cluster, and arming the learned continuity gate by default changed nothing. Recovery here was already fine (10 m) because the longest blackout is 228 s and drift only reached 90 m, within what chi2 alone could re-admit.
2012-08-20.spread_warning: n=2 on 58d7bac: 116.97 (machine in use) and 122.32 (machine idle), 4.57% apart, while the RL control read 10.50 both times, identical. So the variance is the filter's. A move under ~5% here means nothing. Needs more repeats.
2012-08-20.rerun_20261005: REGRESSION on c263814, 2026-10-05: FusionCore 145.192 against a baseline of 116.444 and repeats of 116.97 and 122.32, so +19% to +24% and far outside the 4.57% spread. The RL control read 10.507 against the baseline's 10.519, a move of -0.11%, so the harness is ruled out and this is FusionCore's. Filter rate 101.9 Hz over 4925 s, 5 rl_ekf misses, so not a starved run either. BASELINE DELIBERATELY NOT MOVED: a baseline that is updated to whatever the latest run says cannot detect a regression. This is the #148 territory, where 2012-08-20 was separately measured at 192.923 after 121.669. The sequence now reads 145.192, between the two. The published README figure of 98.3 m is wrong by 1.477x.

2013-04-05.note: 277.6 to 189.7, a 31.7% improvement, reproduced twice (190.028 and 189.388) against two pre-fix runs (275.951 and 279.303), control stable at ~267. This sequence FLIPS from a marginal loss to FusionCore beating RL by 29%. CAUSE, isolated by A/B: not the continuity gate (188.807 with it forced off) but the continuity BUFFER. A buffer spanning a blackout reports mean_dt ~115 s instead of 0.2 s, which feeds min_gap = max(1.0, 2*mean_dt) ~231 s in note_rejection_cascade_start, so any outage SHORTER than that is never classified as a gap and recovery never arms. This sequence has gaps of 275, 129, 65 and 55 s: only the first armed. Recovery after the 129 s gap went 746/750 m to 80/78 m. The 275 s gap is unchanged at ~264 m, which is why the fix first appeared to do nothing here.
2013-04-05.spread_warning: n=2 on 58d7bac: 190.15 and 190.47, 0.17% apart, control 267.42 and 268.68. This sequence repeats tightly, so ~1% is meaningful here where it would be noise on the other two.

_read_this_before_judging_any_regression: The 9x run-to-run spread is NOT universal, which an earlier note here implied. Measured over six unattended runs on 2026-09-12: 2012-06-15 repeats to 2.8%, 2012-08-20 to 4.6%, 2013-04-05 to 1.2%. The historical 32 m to 345 m range was all one sequence, 2013-04-05, and got generalised. So on these sequences a 5 to 10 percent change IS measurable and two runs are enough to see it. Keep the caution for a sequence whose spread has not been measured, and re-check it when adding one. robot_localization remains the control: if it moves more than about a percent between runs, the comparison is void whatever FusionCore did, and that check has already caught one wrong diagnosis (see issue #119).
_rerun_20261005: Re-run of the three sequences with baselines, on c263814, driven strictly sequentially with one playback per sequence feeding BOTH FusionCore and the robot_localization control. Results: 2012-06-15 VALID and confirming (control +0.01%), 2012-08-20 VALID and showing a regression (control -0.11%), 2013-04-05 VOID (control -4.40%, 20 rl_ekf update-rate misses with a worst case of 0.266 s against a 0.05 s budget, and a 75 min playback for 67.5 min of data). The 2013-04-05 arm was contended and is being re-run. NOTE THE PATTERN WORTH CHECKING: both VALID rows overstate FusionCore in the published README by almost exactly the same factor, 1.490x and 1.477x. Two independent sequences landing on the same ratio suggests something systematic rather than independent drift, and it is worth understanding before any published number is rewritten.
_frame_bug_20261006: EVERY ENTRY IN THIS FILE, AND EVERY NCLT NUMBER THIS PROJECT HAS PUBLISHED, WAS MEASURED WITH ISSUE #169 PRESENT. nclt_player.py converted the IMU from NCLT's NED-like body frame to ENU and did not convert the wheel odometry, so the encoder fed a yaw rate of the OPPOSITE SIGN to the gyro for the whole of every run. Proven on 2013-04-05 over 137,509 samples where both sources exceeded 0.08 rad/s: raw odometry against raw gyro disagree 0.0% of the time, raw odometry against the ENU-converted gyro disagree 100.0%, and with the fix they disagree 0.0%. Fixed 2026-10-06. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN: the bug was real and is now gone, but its EFFECT on ATE is UNMEASURED. Do not claim the numbers will improve. The filter never diverged on it because imu.gyro_noise is tighter than encoder.yaw_noise, so it leaned on the gyro and spent gain rejecting the encoder on every turn, a quiet tax rather than a crash. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS FILE: every baseline below is now pre-fix and is not comparable to a post-fix run. check_benchmark_regression.py will read any new run against a pre-fix reference and report nonsense. The whole set needs re-measuring before any of these are used to gate anything again. STILL OPEN AND SEPARATE: the magnitudes do not match either. The median |odom|/|imu| ratio over those same samples is 1.297, so NCLT's own wheel odometry over-reports rotation by about 30%. That is a scale or track-width term, not a frame convention, and the sign fix does not touch it.
